q: 1. The centre of gravity of a semi-circle lies at a distance of ________ from its base measured along the vertical radius.
explain: For a solid semi-circle, the centroidal distance from the base diameter along the axis of symmetry is given by the formula 4r / 3π.

q: 2. The C.G. of a semi-circular arc is at the central radius at a distance of
explain: For a wire bent into a semi-circular arc (line element), the CG is located at 2r/π from the diameter.

q: 3. The C.G. of a quadrant of a circle is at a distance of
explain: The CG of a quarter circle is symmetric and located at a distance of 4r/3π from both bounding radii (axes).

q: 4. M.O.I. of a thin spherical shell of mass M and radius r is given as
explain: The mass moment of inertia of a thin hollow spherical shell about any diameter is (2/3)Mr².

q: 5. The units of moment of inertia of mass are
explain: Mass Moment of Inertia is defined as Σmr², so the unit is mass (kg) times distance squared (m²).

q: 6. Polar moment of inertia of a circle (I₀) is given by
explain: The Polar MI (J or Ip) is the sum of Ixx and Iyy. For a circle: πd⁴/64 + πd⁴/64 = πd⁴/32.

q: 7. Polar moment of inertia is
options: the moment of inertia of an area about an axis parallel to centroidal axis
the moment of an area about an axis which is not lying in the plane of the area
the moment of inertia of an area about a line or axis perpendicular to the plane of the area
explain: By definition, the Polar Moment of Inertia is taken about an axis perpendicular to the cross-section (the Z-axis).

q: 8. The Law "Stress is proportional to strain within elastic limits" is formulated by
explain: Hooke's Law states that within the limit of proportionality, stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 9. Hooke's law holds good up to
explain: While theoretically Hooke's law applies to the limit of proportionality, in many engineering contexts, it is considered valid up to the elastic limit where the linear relationship is mostly maintained.

q: 10. The ratio of linear stress to the linear strain is called
explain: Young's Modulus, or the Modulus of Elasticity (E), is the constant ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain.

q: 11. The unit of modulus of elasticity is same as those of
options: stress, force and modulus of rigidity
stress, pressure and modulus of rigidity
explain: Since strain is dimensionless, the modulus of elasticity (stress/strain) has the same units as stress, pressure, and modulus of rigidity ($N/m^2$ or Pascal).

q: 12. The deformation of a bar under its own weight is ................ the deformation, if the same body is subjected to a direct load equal to the weight of the body.
explain: Deformation under own weight is $WL/2AE$, while deformation under external load W is $WL/AE$. Therefore, self-weight causes half the deformation.

q: 13. The deformation of the bar per unit length in the direction of the force is known as
explain: Linear strain (or longitudinal strain) is defined as the ratio of change in length to the original length in the direction of the applied force.

q: 14. The Young's modulus of a material is 125 GPa and Poisson's ratio 0.25. The modulus of rigidity of the material is
15. The moment of inertia of triangular section b x d, about the base is
explain: Using Parallel Axis Theorem: I_base = I_cg + Ah² = (bh³/36) + (1/2 bh)(h/3)² = bh³/12.

q: 16. When a body is subjected to a direct tensile stress (σ) in one plane, then normal stress on an oblique section... inclined at angle θ to the normal... is
explain: The normal stress on an oblique plane is σ_n = σ cos²θ, where θ is the angle between the normal to the plane and the direction of stress.

q: 17. When a body is subjected to a direct tensile stress (σ) in one plane, then tangential or shear stress on an oblique section... inclined at angle θ to the normal... is
explain: The tangential (shear) stress on an oblique plane is given by τ = (σ/2) sin 2θ.

q: 18. When a body is subjected to a direct tensile stress (σ) in one plane, then maximum normal stress occurs at a section inclined at
explain: Normal stress is σ cos²θ. This is maximum when cos θ = 1, which occurs at θ = 0° (the plane perpendicular to the force).

q: 19. The total strain energy stored in a body is termed as
explain: Resilience is the total strain energy stored in a body within its elastic limit.

q: 20. Resilience is the
options: energy stored in a body when strained within elastic limits
energy stored in a body when strained upto the breaking of the specimen
maximum strain energy which can be stored in a body
explain: as per key d Resilience is the general capacity of a material to absorb energy when it is deformed elastically and release that energy upon unloading.

q: 21. In a stressed body the minimum normal stress at any point is always
options: average of two normal stresses acting in the two principal directions
difference of two normal stresses in the two principal directions plus shear stresses on those planes
explain: As noted in Q. 340, both the maximum and minimum normal stresses are referred to as principal stresses.

q: 22. Glass will obey Hooke's law upto ............
explain: Glass is a perfectly brittle material. It shows almost no plastic deformation and fails (fractures) suddenly while still in the linear elastic range.

q: 23. The limit of eccentricity for no tensile conditions for a column of circular section of diameter (d) is ............
explain: To ensure no tension at any point in a circular section, the load must fall within the middle quarter of the diameter, meaning the eccentricity e ≤ d/8.

q: 24. A tensile test is performed on a round bar. After fracture it has been found that the diameter remains approximately same at fracture. The material under test was ............
explain: Cast iron is a brittle material. It fails by sudden fracture with very little plastic deformation or necking, so the diameter remains nearly unchanged.

q: 25. A column that fails primarily due to direct stress is called
explain: Short columns fail by crushing (direct compressive stress) rather than buckling.

q: 26. A tie is a member which
options: is subjected to axial compression only
is subjected to axial tension only
is subjected to moment tension only
is subjected to two equal and opposite forces
explain: A tie carries axial tension only, as opposed to a strut which carries compression.

q: 27. In simple bending theory, the assumption that plane section before bending remains plane after bending implies that
options: stress is proportional to strain at all sections
strain is proportional to the distance from the natural axis
stress is uniform in the cross-section
explain: The plane-sections assumption directly implies a linear strain distribution across the depth, proportional to distance from the neutral axis.

q: 28. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: Axial load variation along a member's length is plotted as a thrust diagram.

q: 29. A body having similar properties throughout its volume is said to be
explain: Homogeneity means identical properties at every point/volume of the body.

q: 30. The square root of ratio of moment of inertia and cross section area of a member is known as
explain: Radius of gyration k = √(I/A) by definition.

q: 31. Centrifugal force acts at a curve
explain: Centrifugal force is the outward pseudo-force acting away from the center of curvature.

q: 32. The law "Stress is proportional to strain within certain limits" is formulated by
explain: Hooke's Law states stress ∝ strain within the elastic limit.

q: 33. According to Hooke's law which one is correct?
explain: Hooke's Law: stress = Modulus of Elasticity × strain, i.e. σ = Eε.

q: 34. The property of material by which it can be beaten or rolled into plates, is called
explain: Malleability is the ability to be hammered/rolled into thin sheets.

q: 35. The method of increasing fatigue resistance by over stressing the metal by successively increasing the loading is known as
explain: Coaxing improves fatigue strength by applying gradually increasing sub-critical stress cycles.

q: 36. The phenomenon of slow growth of strain under a steady tensile stress, i.e. increasing with time, is called
explain: Creep is time-dependent strain growth under sustained stress.

q: 37. The modular ratio of two materials is defined as (E1 and E2 are the modulus of elasticity of the respective materials)
explain: Modular ratio m = E1/E2, used in composite-section analysis (e.g. RCC transformed sections).

q: 38. How does Young's Modulus vary with increase in temperature?
explain: Interatomic bonding weakens with rising temperature, reducing stiffness (E) for most materials.

q: 39. The stress due to temperature change in a member depends on
explain: Thermal stress only develops if expansion/contraction is restrained — hence it depends on the end/support conditions, not on cross-section or length directly.

q: 40. The ratio of elongations of a conical bar due to its own weight and that of a prismatic bar of the same length is
explain: A conical bar under self-weight elongates only 1/3 as much as a prismatic bar of the same length and weight, due to the tapering cross-section.

q: 41. A member which does not regain its original shape after the load producing deformation is removed, is said to be:
explain: Irrecoverable deformation after unloading is the defining characteristic of plastic behavior.

q: 42. The unit failure stress is taken as:
explain: For design purposes, the ultimate stress is conventionally used as the reference 'failure' stress of the material.

q: 43. The velocity of a moving body is:
explain: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity.

q: 44. The tension in a cable supporting a lift:
options: is more when the lift is moving downwards
is less when the lift is moving upwards
Remains constant whether it moves downwards or upwards
is less when the lift is moving downwards
explain: When a lift accelerates downward, the net upward tension required is less than the static weight (T = m(g − a)).

q: 45. Young's modulus is the ratio of
explain: Young's Modulus E = longitudinal (axial) stress / longitudinal strain.
